name: The centurion of Capernaum
charge: Loving the nation and building the synagogue; not counting himself worthy that the Lord should come under his roof: speak the word only
summary: A centurion at Capernaum had a servant who was dear to him and ready to die, and he sent elders of the Jews to plead for him; they said of him that he loved their nation and had built them their synagogue. He himself sent word that he was not worthy to have Jesus come under his roof, and asked him to say the word only, reasoning from the authority he himself exercised over soldiers and servants. Christ marvelled and said he had not found so great faith, no, not in Israel, and the servant was found whole.
offenseFull: When Christ had ended all his sayings in the audience of the people he entered into Capernaum (Luke 7:1). The verse by verse class begins with where that is, because it settles who the man in this case is. Capernaum lies upon the sea coast in the borders of Zabulon and Nephthalim, the country the prophet calls Galilee of the Gentiles, which is the northern kingdom of Israel and not another nation (Matthew 4:13-16; Isaiah 9:1-2). Christ came there when Nazareth thrust him out (Luke 4:28-31), and he said plainly in that same gospel that he was not sent but to the lost sheep of the house of Israel (Matthew 15:24).

A certain centurion’s servant, who was dear to him, was sick and ready to die, and when he heard of Jesus he sent elders of the Jews to plead for him; and they besought him instantly, saying that the man was worthy for whom he should do this, for he loved their nation and had built them a synagogue (Luke 7:2-5). A centurion is a man set over a hundred soldiers, which is how two of them could be told to make ready two hundred men (Acts 23:23), and this one had the standing and the means to build the people a sanctuary. The class reads him as one of our own, a commandment keeping man of the scattered northern kingdom, and sets him beside Cornelius the centurion of the Italian band, a devout man who feared God with all his house, gave much alms to the people, and whose prayers and alms came up for a memorial before God (Acts 10:1-4). That is the test the class applies: God hears not sinners, but if a man be a worshipper of God and does his will, him he hears (John 9:31). And what both men did with what they had is exactly what the rich are charged to do, not to be highminded nor to trust in uncertain riches, but to be rich in good works, ready to distribute (1 Timothy 6:17-18).

He did not rest the petition on that commendation. When Jesus was not far from the house he sent friends to say that he was not worthy that he should enter under his roof, and that he had not thought himself worthy even to come out to him, but to say in a word, and his servant would be healed. He gave his reason out of the thing he knew: he was himself a man set under authority, having soldiers under him, and he said to one to go and he went, and to another to come and he came, and to his servant to do this and he did it (Luke 7:6-8). The class marks the humility in a man who could move a hundred soldiers and would not walk up to Christ himself: the fear of the Lord is the instruction of wisdom, and before honour is humility (Proverbs 15:33), and all are to be subject one to another and clothed with humility, because God resists the proud and gives grace to the humble (1 Peter 5:5-6).
judgmentFull: When Jesus heard these things he marvelled at him, and turned about and said to the people that followed him that he had not found so great faith, no, not in Israel (Luke 7:9). They that were sent returned to the house and found the servant whole that had been sick (Luke 7:10), and Matthew sets down that he was healed in the selfsame hour (Matthew 8:13). The class answers the reading that makes this a heathen praised above Israel: the town is in Zabulon and Nephthalim, the elders of the Jews carried his petition, and he had built the synagogue the nation worshipped in.

Matthew tells the same account with the centurion himself speaking to Christ (Matthew 8:5-10), and the class settles the apparent contradiction with a rule taken out of the record itself. What one man does by another, he does by himself. The friends and the servants who carried the words were the very men he commanded to go and to come, so the words are his words whoever carried them; and the Lord said he would save his people Israel out of the hand of the Philistines by the hand of his servant David, though David did it with an army under him (2 Samuel 3:18).
What is praised here is the faith, and what answered it was a word spoken at a distance, to a house Christ never entered.

text.text: Now when he had ended all his sayings in the audience of the people, he entered into Capernaum.
And leaving Nazareth, he came and dwelt in Capernaum, which is upon the sea coast, in the borders of Zabulon and Nephthalim:
That it might be fulfilled which was spoken by Esaias the prophet, saying,
The land of Zabulon, and the land of Nephthalim, by the way of the sea, beyond Jordan, Galilee of the Gentiles;
The people which sat in darkness saw great light; and to them which sat in the region and shadow of death light is sprung up.

Nevertheless the dimness shall not be such as was in her vexation, when at the first he lightly afflicted the land of Zebulun and the land of Naphtali, and afterward did more grievously afflict her by the way of the sea, beyond Jordan, in Galilee of the nations.
The people that walked in darkness have seen a great light: they that dwell in the land of the shadow of death, upon them hath the light shined.
And all they in the synagogue, when they heard these things, were filled with wrath,
And rose up, and thrust him out of the city, and led him unto the brow of the hill whereon their city was built, that they might cast him down headlong.
But he passing through the midst of them went his way,
And came down to Capernaum, a city of Galilee, and taught them on the sabbath days.
But he answered and said, I am not sent but unto the lost sheep of the house of Israel.
And a certain centurion’s servant, who was dear unto him, was sick, and ready to die.
And when he heard of Jesus, he sent unto him the elders of the Jews, beseeching him that he would come and heal his servant.
And when they came to Jesus, they besought him instantly, saying, That he was worthy for whom he should do this:
For he loveth our nation, and he hath built us a synagogue.
And he called unto him two centurions, saying, Make ready two hundred soldiers to go to Cesarea, and horsemen threescore and ten, and spearmen two hundred, at the third hour of the night;
There was a certain man in Cesarea called Cornelius, a centurion of the band called the Italian band,
A devout man, and one that feared God with all his house, which gave much alms to the people, and prayed to God alway.
He saw in a vision evidently about the ninth hour of the day an angel of God coming in to him, and saying unto him, Cornelius.
And when he looked on him, he was afraid, and said, What is it, Lord? And he said unto him, Thy prayers and thine alms are come up for a memorial before God.
Now we know that God heareth not sinners: but if any man be a worshipper of God, and doeth his will, him he heareth.
Charge them that are rich in this world, that they be not highminded, nor trust in uncertain riches, but in the living God, who giveth us richly all things to enjoy;
That they do good, that they be rich in good works, ready to distribute, willing to communicate;

Then Jesus went with them. And when he was now not far from the house, the centurion sent friends to him, saying unto him, Lord, trouble not thyself: for I am not worthy that thou shouldest enter under my roof:
Wherefore neither thought I myself worthy to come unto thee: but say in a word, and my servant shall be healed.
For I also am a man set under authority, having under me soldiers, and I say unto one, Go, and he goeth; and to another, Come, and he cometh; and to my servant, Do this, and he doeth it.
The fear of the Lord is the instruction of wisdom; and before honour is humility.
Likewise, ye younger, submit yourselves unto the elder. Yea, all of you be subject one to another, and be clothed with humility: for God resisteth the proud, and giveth grace to the humble.
Humble yourselves therefore under the mighty hand of God, that he may exalt you in due time:
When Jesus heard these things, he marvelled at him, and turned him about, and said unto the people that followed him, I say unto you, I have not found so great faith, no, not in Israel.
And they that were sent, returning to the house, found the servant whole that had been sick.
And Jesus said unto the centurion, Go thy way; and as thou hast believed, so be it done unto thee. And his servant was healed in the selfsame hour.
And when Jesus was entered into Capernaum, there came unto him a centurion, beseeching him,
And saying, Lord, my servant lieth at home sick of the palsy, grievously tormented.
And Jesus saith unto him, I will come and heal him.
The centurion answered and said, Lord, I am not worthy that thou shouldest come under my roof: but speak the word only, and my servant shall be healed.
For I am a man under authority, having soldiers under me: and I say to this man, Go, and he goeth; and to another, Come, and he cometh; and to my servant, Do this, and he doeth it.
When Jesus heard it, he marvelled, and said to them that followed, Verily I say unto you, I have not found so great faith, no, not in Israel.
Now then do it: for the Lord hath spoken of David, saying, By the hand of my servant David I will save my people Israel out of the hand of the Philistines, and out of the hand of all their enemies.
And I will bless them that bless thee, and curse him that curseth thee: and in thee shall all families of the earth be blessed.

Also the sons of the stranger, that join themselves to the Lord, to serve him, and to love the name of the Lord, to be his servants, every one that keepeth the sabbath from polluting it, and taketh hold of my covenant;

Even them will I bring to my holy mountain, and make them joyful in my house of prayer: their burnt offerings and their sacrifices shall be accepted upon mine altar; for mine house shall be called an house of prayer for all people.
